Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Fresh read on objectui `origin/main` `c2191654a4`.

- **The premise holds as code-read:** `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:2343` `executeForm(action)` takes only the action, and the bridge (`RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx`) puts the row on the action definition. The measurement is the card's: 3 rows, 3 fresh loads.
- **p1:** the item fails, so its P1 is the upper bound. The failure form is a wall: "Log Time" from a related row opens a blank CREATE form instead of the row's edit form, so the action cannot do its job from that position.
- **Lane `domain:ui`:** carry the row's record context into `executeForm` (as the `record_section` leg does since #4278). Pin a `type: form` action fired from a related row opening that row.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `eabce85cf175ea26258099839934f0a104531775`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #13063 (body, the triage comment, the claim as amended, the os-dev-report), PR #13073 (body, 5 files, net diff against `main` at `fb85637e14`), the check-runs on the head, and the head's source of `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, `packages/core/src/actions/index.ts`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx` and `packages/react/src/context/ActionContext.tsx` (read only, through the GitHub contents API). The showcase's `record_related` placements were read from `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts` in the objectstack checkout.

### ① Derived judgments

Public-surface change: `ActionRunner.execute(action: ActionDef)` becomes `execute(action, callContext?: Partial of ActionContext)`. `ActionRunner` reaches `@object-ui/core`'s public face through `export * from './ActionRunner.js'` in the actions barrel, so this is a widening of a published method. No new export, no new file under `src/` other than tests. Right.

- **A caller passing no `callContext` is unchanged.** The only inserted statement in the old path is `if (callContext) return this.scopedTo(callContext).execute(action);` ahead of the existing `try`. With the argument absent the branch is not taken and the body that follows is byte-for-byte the previous `execute`. The bridge passes `undefined` when the row is not an object, which takes that same unchanged path. The provider's own `execute` wrapper still calls `runner.execute(action)` with one argument. Right.

- **The one-shot runner shares every handler the original holds.** The class fields at head are `handlers`, `scripts`, `evaluator`, `context`, `confirmHandler`, `toastHandler`, `modalHandler`, `navigationHandler`, `paramCollectionHandler`, `resultDialogHandler`, `translate`, and the readonly `builtinExecutors`. `scopedTo` assigns the two Maps by reference and the six handlers plus `translate` by value. Not copied: `context` (replaced by the merged one, by design), `evaluator` (rebuilt by the constructor over the merged context, which is the point: the evaluator must read the row), and `builtinExecutors` (a per-instance table of arrow functions bound to `this`, so the fresh instance's own table dispatches to the fresh instance's executors; copying it would be wrong). Because the Maps are shared by reference, a handler registered on the original after the scoped runner is built is still seen. The constructor applies `withIdentityAlias` to the merged bag, so `os.user` is re-derived from `user`; the test pins it. `current_user`, which the provider binds through `updateContext`, lives on `this.context` and so is carried by the spread. Nothing a dispatch path reads is missing. Right.

- **Dropping `objectFields` / `objectActions` on an object change is right.** Every reader of those two keys at head is `readContextObjectFields` / `readContextObjectActions`, which answer only when `readContextObjectName(context) === objectName`. On the shared runner a retargeted row action (`action.objectName` = child, context = parent) therefore already got `undefined` for both. On the scoped runner the context now names the child, so without the drop the parent's field map and declarations would answer for the child; the drop restores the same `undefined` the update path and `declaredUpdatePatch` saw before. When `callContext` names the same object (a self-relation) the pair is kept, which is the correct reading, and the test pins both branches. The `ctx` mirror gets the same treatment so `${ctx.record.*}` and `${record.*}` agree. Right.

- **`executeForm` still ignores `action.objectName` (objectui#4292).** The method is untouched in the diff and at head reads `recordId` from `this.context.record` / `this.context.data` and the object from `readContextObjectName(this.context)` only. The scoped runner's `this.context` names the row and the child, which is exactly the shape a dispatch from the child's own record page has. The ban holds. Right.

- **`update` / `api` / `flow` / `script` unchanged; url and navigation templates now bind the row.** Confirmed by reading the head: `executeUpdateOperation` takes `action.objectName || readContextObjectName(...)` and the row from `params._rowRecord`; the console's `api` / `flow` / `script` handlers read `action.objectName`, `action.recordId`, `params.recordId` and `_rowRecord` from the definition before any context, and the bridge still writes all of these on the definition (pinned by the `api` control). The row runs with a context that now also names the row, which is additive for those handlers. `navigateTo` evaluates `${record.*}` through `this.evaluator` and `${ctx.recordId}` through `buildInterpolationContext` (`this.context.record?.id ?? this.context.recordId`, then the `ctx` mirror merged on top); on the scoped runner both resolve to the row. The record page's provider context carries `record`, `objectName`, `objectFields` and no flat `recordId`, so the mirror does not re-introduce the parent's id. Safety for existing authored `record_related` url actions: the ruling (triage comment and the card's expected fix shape) sanctions the row as the execution context, so a url template at that location reading the parent was relying on the defect; the showcase declares exactly one action at `record_related` (`showcase_log_time`, `type: form`) and no url template there, so no shipped example changes meaning. The change is correct and bounded. One further consequence the dev did not list, same direction: the runner's own `executeAPI` fallback (no registered `api` handler) builds its body from `action.params ?? this.context.data`, which `callContext` does not touch, so it is unchanged. Right.

- **Bypassing `ActionProvider`'s execute wrapper is not a user-visible regression.** The wrapper only sets the provider's `loading` / `error` / `result` state and catches a throw; the loading indicator and the error or success toast a user sees come from the runner itself (`handlePostExecution` through the shared `toastHandler`, the shared `confirmHandler`, the shared `paramCollectionHandler`), all of which the scoped runner holds. `runner.execute` has its own `try`/`catch` returning `{ success: false, error }`, so the wrapper's catch adds nothing for this path. Measured at head: the only non-test `useAction()` consumers that destructure anything beyond `execute` / `updateContext` / `runner` are none (`useObjectActions` reads `loading` / `error` from `useActionRunner`, a separate hook); `empty-state-link.tsx` already dispatches through `useAction().runner` directly, so the shape has a precedent. The one observable difference is that the provider no longer re-renders its subtree for a related-row dispatch, which nothing depends on. Right; carried forward under ③ as the dev flagged it.

- Smaller points, all right: the `[runner]` dependency replaces `[execute]` and `runner` is memoised on the serialised context, so `runRowAction` is as stable as before; `'objectName' in callContext` with a base context lacking `objectName` reads as changed and drops a pair that is absent anyway; the fallback `useAction()` (no provider) builds a fresh runner each render, which was equally true of the old `execute` and is not a regression.

Tests: the app-shell pin mounts the real provider, bridge, renderer and related list and observes the navigation handler, with three controls (child record page, page-level parent action after a row dispatch, a non-form row action); the ablation reported in the PR body turns the defect case and the `api` context assertion red and leaves the controls green. The core pin covers the merge, one-shot-ness, handler sharing, the alias, the mirror and the pair drop. No test is modified or deleted.

Check-runs on `eabce85cf175`: `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `label` and `Live E2E (informational)` are success; `Test (coverage)` and the coverage shards are skipped by design. Still in progress at the time of this record: `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Repo Gates`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Test (dist pins)` and the sixteen `Test (shard n/16)` jobs. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts for those families; this record does not wait for them, and the PASS below is conditional on none of them concluding failure.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/13063-related-row-form-action.md` declares `@object-ui/core: minor` and `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. Both packages have `src/` edits in the fixed group, so `check-changeset-presence` requires a declaration, and one is present (the `Changeset Declaration` run is green). `minor` on core is right: a widened signature of a published method is an additive public-surface change, and the objectui#12967 precedent plus the AGENTS.md rule that objectui never declares `major` make `minor` the ceiling as well as the floor. `patch` on app-shell is right: the bridge's change is a behaviour fix behind an unchanged component API. `check-changeset-no-major` is green. The body names the widened method and states that the argument is optional, which matches the diff. `Clause-②: yes` in the PR body matches the amended claim and the fact that a published method's signature changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report's `open_questions` is empty. Dev flags and out-of-scope findings:

1. Bypass of the provider's execute wrapper (`loading` / `error` / `result` not set for related-row dispatches), carrier none. Judged under ① as not a regression; the suggested follow-up (an optional second argument on the provider's `execute`) belongs to `@object-ui/react`, outside this card's file surface, and needs no card to land this fix. Answered.
2. url / navigation row templates now bind the row. Judged under ① as the ruling's sanctioned change with no shipped example affected. The dev added no separate url pin; the `form` pin covers the same context path, which is acceptable at this tier. Answered.
3. `check:spec-floors` exit 1 `no-artifact` locally (needs a whole-workspace build). That family is answered by the head's `Repo Gates` / `Build & E2E` runs, still in progress above. Answered as far as this record can.
4. Out-of-scope: a `type: form` action at `list_item` fired from an object list row (no record in the runner context) opens bare `/forms/NAME` by the same mechanism; code-read only, not reproduced, not filed. Not this card's defect and not introduced here; the new `callContext` is the natural carrier for that fix. Escalated to the seat as a candidate card, no action required on this PR.
5. Minor: the PR body's verification section names head `3dafcd4657`, two commits before the reviewed head `eabce85cf1`; the diff reviewed here is the net diff at the reviewed head, and the check-runs quoted are on it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-13063-related-row-form-action`
Reviewed-by: `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## ACCEPT · objectui#13063 · PR #13073 · `domain:ui#2` · `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB` · 2026-10-19T19:13Z

PR #13073 at head `eabce85` (`Fixes #13063`, `Clause-②: yes`). Reviewed against:
- the claim `6274196031`, amended to Clause-② yes because `ActionRunner` is published;
- triage `6273652415`;
- the dev report `6274878854` plus the changeset round;
- the contract review **PASS** `6275047442`.

- **Premise:** holds. `RelatedRecordActionsBridge` retargeted a row action through the definition only, while `executeForm` reads the record and object from the runner context (the parent page). So "Log Time" on a related row opened a blank create form.
- **Diff read by the seat:**
  - `ActionRunner.execute(action, callContext?)`: with a `callContext`, it runs once on a scoped runner over the merged context. That runner shares every handler and registry by reference. The ctx mirror follows the merge, and `objectFields` / `objectActions` are dropped when the object changes.
  - Without `callContext`, `execute` is byte-for-byte unchanged.
  - The bridge passes `{ record: row, objectName: CHILD }`. The definition keeps `objectName` / `recordId` / `_rowRecord`, so the `update`, `api`, `flow` and `script` handlers are unchanged.
  - `executeForm` still ignores `action.objectName` (objectui#4292).
  - url / navigation templates at `record_related` now bind the row. That is the ruling's sanctioned change, and no shipped example reads the parent there.
- **Changeset:** `@object-ui/core` `minor` (a widened published method; objectui#12967 precedent) and `@object-ui/app-shell` `patch`.
- **Pins:**
  - `RelatedRecordActionsBridge.rowFormContext-13063` (real provider, bridge and related list; controls: the child record page, a page-level parent action after a row dispatch, an `api` row action).
  - `ActionRunner.callContext-13063` (merge, one-shot, handler sharing, alias, mirror, pair drop).
  - Ablation: with the row on the definition only, (a) received `/forms/task.edit`. Restored by blob hash.
- **Local gates:** a 52-file union, 604 tests; closure build and type-check for core and app-shell; `eslint` 0 errors; the battery and changeset checks all 0.
- **Acceptance notes (not filed):**
  - A related-row dispatch bypasses `ActionProvider`'s loading / error / result wrapper. No `useAction()` consumer reads it, and toasts, confirm and params come from the shared runner (judged no regression).
  - A `type: form` action at `list_item` fired from an object-list row has the same blank-form mechanism. That is code-read only, with no public-door reproduction, so it is not filed; the new `callContext` is its natural carrier.
- **Commits:** model-free trailers. The PR went through the fleet-write relay.
- **CI at head:** 36/36 check-runs success or skipped on `eabce85` (filter=latest), `mergeable_state` clean.

Verdict: **ACCEPT**. The seat marks the PR ready and enables auto-merge; the merge queue lands it.
